misconceptions.description: Treating text contrast as an aesthetic preference rather than a measurable WCAG threshold
misconceptions.trigger: learner defends low-contrast text as a clean look without checking the ratio
misconceptions.feedback: Measure the contrast ratio against the AA threshold (4.5:1 for body text). Contrast is a pass or fail check, not a taste call.

misconceptions.description: Assuming an image is accessible because any alt text exists, regardless of whether it conveys the content
misconceptions.trigger: alt text is generic such as image or photo and carries none of the informational content
misconceptions.feedback: Write alt text that conveys the information the image carries in context. Presence is not the same as a usable description.

misconceptions.description: Accepting AI-generated alt text that describes appearance but misses the image's instructional role
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes AI alt text without checking it against why the image is on the page
misconceptions.feedback: Check each AI description against what the image must communicate in the lesson. Appearance is not the same as instructional meaning.

misconceptions.description: Using color as the only channel for status or meaning, excluding users with color vision deficiency
misconceptions.trigger: correct and incorrect or other states differ only by color
misconceptions.feedback: Pair color with text or a distinct shape so the meaning is perceivable without color discrimination.
